title: The v3 CSS Entry Point
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of the v3 css entry point.
Apply one appropriate technique to a small Tailwind CSS example.
Verify the expected result and identify a common failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, focus on the v3 css entry point and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: The v3 CSS Entry Point protects existing projects from accidental regressions when framework versions and build workflows differ.

content_blocks.title: Module 20 learning map
content_blocks.alt_text: Four-step module learning map: Understanding Tailwind CSS v3 Configuration → Migrating Installation and Build Tooling → Migrating Source Detection and Safelisting → Maintaining Older Tailwind Projects. Lesson pages add code examples and practice.
content_blocks.caption: Learning map for Module 20, from the opening concept to a practical checkpoint.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: The @tailwind directives; Base, component, and utility layers; Preflight behavior; Custom CSS within v3 layers; Understanding older project stylesheets. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: The v3 CSS Entry Point
content_blocks.expected_output: In a v3 project, these directives mark the layers processed by the v3 build pipeline.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to the v3 css entry point, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Create a minimal example demonstrating the v3 css entry point. Include a before/after comparison and explain why the chosen utility, variant or directive is appropriate.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to the v3 css entry point.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to the v3 css entry point.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: In a v3 project, these directives mark the layers processed by the v3 build pipeline.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying the v3 css entry point without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: The v3 CSS Entry Point is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
